title: Predicting Task Difficulty Without Rollouts
abstract: arXiv:2608.05797v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: A fundamental challenge in evaluating and training autonomous agents is measuring the intrinsic difficulty of the tasks they attempt. Estimating this quantity can be useful for environment designers creating synthetic data or benchmarks, as well as for constructing training curricula, thereby offering a way to reduce compute costs. Such an estimation becomes increasingly important as agents (particularly LLM-based) move into longer-horizon domains, where empirical trial-and-error becomes a severe computational bottleneck. However existing work is largely confined to static tasks and relies on evaluation metrics that, as we show, can give an incomplete picture of predictive performance. In this paper we study ex ante difficulty prediction across 17 agentic benchmarks spanning coding, mathematics, machine learning, web navigation, function calling, and other domains. translated_title: 无需滚动模拟的任务难度预测
translated_abstract: 评估和训练自主智能体的一个根本挑战，是衡量它们所尝试任务的内在难度。对这一指标的估计对于创建合成数据或基准的环境设计者，以及构建训练课程都非常有用，从而提供了一种降低计算成本的途径。随着智能体（尤其是基于大语言模型的智能体）进入更长时程的领域，这种估计变得愈发重要，因为经验性的试错会成为严重的计算瓶颈。然而，现有工作大多局限于静态任务，并且所依赖的评估指标——正如我们所展示的——可能无法完整反映预测性能。在本文中，我们研究了涵盖编码、数学、机器学习、网页导航、函数调用及其他领域的17个智能体基准上的事前（ex ante）难度预测。我们发现，AUC可能掩盖较差的难度估计，并识别出……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出无需实际运行智能体（rollout）即可在覆盖编码、数学、网页导航等17个智能体基准上进行事前任务难度预测，从而降低试错带来的计算成本，并揭示AUC等常用指标可能掩盖较差的难度估计。
en_tdlr: This paper presents an ex ante approach to predicting intrinsic task difficulty across 17 agentic benchmarks—spanning coding, math, web navigation, and more—without costly rollouts, and shows that AUC can mask poor difficulty estimates.
